backstory.text:
You trained as a soldier on the island of Mintarn and joined a mercenary company. You traveled to the city of Neverwinter with your company to serve in both the army and city watch. Over time, you grew disillusioned with many of your fellow soldiers. They seemed to enjoy their authority at the expense of the people they’re supposed to protect. 

Recently you’ve had dreams of a shadow creeping across the sea like a shroud, swallowing an island in darkness. Though you dismissed the dreams at first, you began to hear a voice calling you to stand against death’s endless hunger. Certain of your deity’s wishes, you resigned your post and set out on your quest.

You spent years learning the lore of the multiverse. You scoured manuscripts, studied scrolls, and listened to the greatest experts on the subjects that interest you. Your efforts have made you a master researcher.

backstory.text:
Your family is no stranger to wealth, power, and privilege. In the glory days of Neverwinter, your parents ruled the county of Corlinn Hill, located in the hills northeast of the city. But Mount Hotenow erupted thirty years ago, devastating Neverwinter and erasing Corlinn Hill. Instead of growing up on an estate, you were raised in a small townhouse in Waterdeep. As an adult, you stand to inherit only a title. 

Since swearing your oath to Bahamut, you’ve returned to Neverwinter and have been a champion to those who are overlooked by the institutions that exist to protect them. Recently, your resolve has been shaken by corruption in the city guard and ruling aristocrats.

Born in a quiet halfling village, you were always too curious for your own good. Locks were puzzles to be solved, and secrets were treasures to be uncovered. That curiosity eventually led you into the city’s underbelly, where you learned the arts of disguise, deception, and the quick hand of a thief. For a time, you worked as a spy-for-hire, slipping through shadows and gathering secrets for coin. But after a job went wrong — a mark discovered, a friend betrayed, a secret stolen too well — you had to disappear. Now you travel under a new name, smiling and joking like the world’s on your side, but always watching from the corner of the room. Whether your past will catch up to you or not is uncertain, but until then, you’re content to slip through the world as the party’s unseen shadow.

appearance.text: Wood elves’ skin tends to be copperish in hue, sometimes with traces of green. Their hair tends toward browns and blacks, but it is occasionally blond or copper-colored. Their eyes are green, brown, or hazel.

backstory.text:
Early Life — The Greenwood Son 
Vadania was born beneath the emerald canopy of an ancient forest settlement known as Tel’Quessiriel, a quiet wood elf enclave hidden where the trees grow impossibly tall, and the light falls in soft green-gold shafts. The Amakiir family were wardens of the outer glades — not nobles, not warriors of renown, but trusted guardians of the balance between civilization and wild. 
His mother, Lethariel, was a healer who spoke to plants as if they were old friends. 
His father, Thalion Amakiir, taught Vadania how to read broken twigs like pages in a book. 

From childhood, Vadania preferred the hush of the wild to village chatter. He could track deer before he could braid his own hair. By 40 (barely adolescence for an elf), he could loose two arrows before most could draw one. 

He believed his life would always be this simple: 
	•	Guard the borders. 
	•	Protect the herd paths. 
	•	Return home to warm lamplight and laughter. 

He was wrong. 

The Night of Cinders 
The bandits did not come like fools crashing through the brush.  They came guided.  Someone knew the old paths. Someone knew the watch rotations. Someone knew where the alarm glyphs were weakest.  Vadania was on the western ridge when the first smoke rose. 
By the time he returned, the village was ash and screaming. These were not starving highwaymen — they carried alchemist’s fire, iron nets, and silvered blades. They hunted elves specifically. 

He found he father among the fallen, still clutching a snapped bowstring. His mother’s healing satchel lay torn and blood-soaked.  Vadania survived because he was away.  That truth claws at he still.
